item.title: Tinubu concludes Saudi Arabia visit, says he prayed for Nigeria
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has concluded his visit to Saudi Arabia, where he performed the lesser Hajj, known as Umrah, and entered the Holy Kaaba to offer prayers. Tinubu disclosed this in a statement following the visit, expressing gratitude to Saudi Arabia’s King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud and Crown Prince and Prime Minister Mohammed bin Salman for granting him and members of his delegation the privilege. The President also appreciated the Saudi leadership for its hospitality and support, describing the gesture as a reflection of the longstanding relationship between Nigeria and the Kingdom. He said he used the opportunity to pray for peace, unity and prosperity in Nigeria. “I have concluded my visit to the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, where, together with members of my delegation, I had the rare honour of entering the Holy Kaaba to pray, and of performing Umrah. “I am deeply grateful to the Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques, King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, and to Crown Prince and Prime Minister Mohammed bin Salman for extending this privilege to us, and for their gracious hospitality and brotherly care. It reflects the enduring bonds of faith and friendship between Nigeria and Saudi Arabia. “In those sacred moments, I prayed for peace, unity and prosperity for our dear nation and for all Nigerians,” He wrote. The post Tinubu concludes Saudi Arabia visit, says he prayed for Nigeria appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Sokoto SSANU begins warning strike over unpaid entitlements
item.description: ….Union threatens indefinite shutdown if demands remain unmet By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto SOKOTO — The Senior Staff Association of Nigerian Universities (SSANU), Sokoto State University (SSU) chapter, has commenced a five-working-day warning strike over outstanding staff entitlements, threatening an indefinite shutdown if the dispute with the Sokoto State Government is not resolved. The union said the industrial action followed the expiration of a 14-working-day ultimatum issued to the state government over its demands. In a statement signed by its Chairman, Ismail Bala Muhammed, and Secretary, Mansur Ahmad, SSANU said the strike was triggered by the government’s failure to approve and implement the outstanding entitlements despite repeated engagements. The association said it initially submitted its demands through the appropriate channels before forwarding a comprehensive document on July 28, 2026, following the agreement between the Federal Government and the union on the 35 per cent Consolidated Non-Teaching Tools Allowance (CONTTA). It said it subsequently made several verbal and written appeals, including visits to the Commissioner for Higher Education, the Permanent Secretary of the ministry and the Deputy Governor, in a bid to secure an amicable settlement. Following the engagements, the state government constituted a committee comprising the Commissioner for Higher Education, the Permanent Secretary, the Deputy Accountant-General and Professor Mustapha Aliyu to engage representatives of SSANU, the National Association of Academic Technologists (NAAT) and the Non-Academic Staff Union (NASU) from SSU and Shehu Shagari University of Education. At a meeting on October 9, the government communicated its position on the outstanding claims. However, SSANU said the response failed to address its members’ major concerns. According to the union, the government rejected payment of arrears arising from the 25 per cent salary increment, proposed implementing CONTTA from January 2027 subject to budgetary provision, and maintained that annual salary increments had already been implemented. Dissatisfied with the outcome, SSANU said it convened an emergency congress on October 13, where members resolved to issue a 14-working-day ultimatum to the government. The union warned that failure to meet its demands would trigger a five-day warning strike and potentially an indefinite industrial action. It, however, temporarily suspended the planned announcement of the strike after the Permanent Secretary scheduled a meeting with representatives of SSANU from SSU and Shehu Shagari University of Education on October 14. At the meeting, the Permanent Secretary reportedly disclosed that the governor had directed the unions to resubmit their demands, separating existing claims from new ones and indicating their respective financial implications. item.title: NASS Considering Proposal To Create 74 Seats For Women, Says Bamidele
item.description: Leader of the Senate, Senator Opeyemi Bamidele, on Monday disclosed that the National Assembly Committee on the Review of the 1999 Constitution (as amended) had proposed the creation of 74 additional seats for women in the Senate and House of Representatives Bamidele, also Vice Chairman, Senate Committee on the Review of the 1999 Constitution, further revealed that the committee had proposed three additional seats in each State House of Assembly, all specifically reserved for women, without displacing any existing electoral seats. He made this disclosure at the 2026 Law Week organised by the International Federation of Women Lawyers (FIDA), Ekiti State Chapter on Monday, noting that the proposals were designed to deepen the inclusion of women in the country’s politics and governance process. A file photo of Senator Opeyemi Bamidele Ekiti FIDA, chaired by Mrs. Ayobami Olowoyo-Richards, organised the programme with the theme, “Justice in a Changing World: Responding to New Challenges Affecting Women and Children.” Bamidele attended the programme alongside the Chairman, House of Representatives Committee on Information and National Orientation, Steve Fatoba, and Speaker, Ekiti State House of Assembly, Adeoye Aribasoye, among others. “A Bill for an Act to alter the provisions of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 to provide for special seats for women in the National and State Houses of Assembly and for related matters is receiving our attention at the National Assembly,” Bamidele said. He further explained the centerpiece of the legislative initiative, which, according to him, was designed to create special seats for women at the National Assembly and State Houses of Assembly under the ongoing review of the 1999 Constitution. He added that the legislative initiative “is the fruit of extensive consultation and consensus-building. “It is why we commenced the constitutional amendment process early, ensuring that this is not a rushed, haphazard endeavour but a deliberate, inclusive, and thorough reform. “The proposal, as it stands, is meticulous in its design. It seeks to add 37 seats in the Senate and 37 seats in the House of Representatives. This suggests that if finally approved, each state of the federation, including FCT, will have one additional seat in each of the Houses of the National Assembly,” he added. Bamidele further revealed that the constitution review committee “has already proposed three additional seats for each state House of Assembly, all specifically reserved for women, without displacing any existing electoral seats. “This arrangement is proposed to run for a period of 16 years, four electoral cycles, before a comprehensive review. item.title: Otti: Abia won’t celebrate thieves, drug barons again
item.description: …Governor honours Emeritus Professor Oluikpe at 90 By Steve Oko UMUAHIA — Abia State Governor, Alex Otti, has said his administration is working to dismantle what he described as a culture of celebrating thieves, fraudsters, drug barons and other questionable characters, insisting that public recognition should be reserved for people of integrity and genuine accomplishments. Otti spoke at the 90th birthday celebration of Emeritus Professor Benson Oluikpe in Umuahia, where he said his administration was institutionalising the celebration of excellence to inspire younger generations to pursue worthy achievements. “We want to depart from that inherited culture. It’s not our culture. Culture of celebrating thieves. Culture of celebrating 419-ers. Culture of celebrating drug barons. Culture of celebrating bandits. That’s not our culture. That’s not how we grew up,” the governor said. He faulted the practice of honouring outstanding individuals only after their death, when they could no longer enjoy the recognition, saying achievers should be celebrated while alive. According to him, recognising people for their contributions would encourage others, particularly young people, to aspire to excellence. Otti cited the recent celebration of five Abia schoolchildren who emerged champions at an international competition in Qatar, saying his administration was determined to make excellence, rather than questionable wealth and influence, the basis for public recognition. The governor also used a personal experience to illustrate the importance of accountability, recalling how his father questioned him in 1989 over the source of the N100 he sent home while working at Citibank. He said he had earned the money through extra work and daily allowances, but his father insisted on knowing how he legitimately made it. “That’s how I was brought up. You needed to give account. But these days, people don’t ask questions. We need to go back to that time when we would ask questions. Ask your children questions. Let them give account,” he said. Otti maintained that people’s values, rather than the times, had changed, citing his son’s decision to provide receipts and explanations for money he had saved towards buying a house in the United States. Earlier, Oluikpe expressed gratitude for the honour and prayed for God’s blessings on the governor. “You have honoured me; may God honour you,” the nonagenarian said. The professor, who disclosed that he first met Otti in 2013 when the governor was still a banker, described him as a humble man endowed with wisdom. He said the impression he formed of Otti during their first encounter influenced his subsequent support for the governor’s political ambition. Recounting how Otti once stood up to return an award to him at a public function, Oluikpe said the gesture demonstrated a humility that had remained consistent in the governor’s public life. item.title: 2027: Niger Delta Youths slam Uzodinma’s aide over attack on Wike
item.description: By Ugochukwu Alaribe UMUAHIA -A political group,Niger Delta Youth Movement, NDYM, has warned an aide to Governor Hope Uzodinma,Mr. Collins Opurozor,to stop attacking the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory,FCT, Nyesom Wike over the senatorial tussle between the Governor and Owelle Rochas Okorocha. The group also urged Opurozor not to use the disagreement between the two APC Chieftains to create hostility between the South East zone and Wike. The group alleged that Opurozor has been attempting to undermine Wike through inflammatory political remarks. The Movement declared that it would not continue to watch Opurozor attack the FCT Minister without consequences and urged him to exercise restraint and desist from using media interviews to settle political scores. In a statement by its Publicity Secretary, Comrade Jeffery Nwali, NDYM condemned Opurozor’s comments on a national television where he accused Wike of attempting to turn the South East into his personal political fiefdom by allegedly encouraging the emergence of weak leaders in the region to preserve his political influence. Describing the comments as reckless and provocative,the group,however, insisted that Wike’s political engagements should not be misrepresented as an attack on Igbo interests. The statement read;”We condemn the attempt by Collins Opurozor to drag the FCT Minister into Imo State’s political disputes, particularly following the Federal High Court judgment concerning Governor Uzodinma’s APC senatorial candidacy in Imo West senatorial zone. “Disagreements between Uzodinma and other political actors in Imo State should not be allowed to create unnecessary hostility between the South East and the FCT Minister. “During the television interview, Opurozor strongly criticized the judgment, dismissed Senator Samuel Anyanwu over what he described as his lack of grassroots support in Imo State, and berated the administration of former Governor Rochas Okorocha as too disgraceful to be remembered. “He also accused Wike of undermining Igbo political interests by allegedly supporting political figures opposed to Uzodinma. “Collins Opurozor is a young political aide who over- rates his intelligence and mistakes verbal aggression for political sophistication. Political disagreements should not become excuses to denigrate established political leaders.” The post 2027: Niger Delta Youths slam Uzodinma’s aide over attack on Wike appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Nigeria targets wider access to West African markets
item.description: … FG urges businesses to exploit ECOWAS trade scheme By Boluwaji Obahopo, Lokoja LOKOJA — The Federal Government has urged Nigerian manufacturers, farmers and entrepreneurs to take advantage of the ECOWAS Trade Liberalisation Scheme (ETLS) to expand their businesses into West African markets. The government said increased regional trade was critical to economic growth, integration and stability across the sub-region. The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Ambassador Sola Enikanolaiye, made the call at the ECOWAS Trade Liberalisation Scheme Sensitisation Workshop for the North-Central zone, held in Lokoja, Kogi State, in collaboration with the ECOWAS Commission. Enikanolaiye disclosed that Nigeria had registered about 3,500 companies and 20,000 products under the scheme, but said the figures remained below the country’s potential compared with the performance of some other ECOWAS member states. He urged Nigerian businesses to exploit the scheme, which grants qualifying products originating from member countries preferential access to regional markets, to increase exports, expand production and improve the country’s competitiveness. The minister identified the agricultural potential of Kogi and other North-Central states as an opportunity to develop products for regional and international markets. He listed livestock, mangoes, millet, maize, sugar, groundnuts and cashew as commodities that could be processed into value-added products for export to other West African countries. Enikanolaiye urged participants to use the workshop to familiarise themselves with product registration procedures, rules of origin, certification and other requirements for accessing preferential markets under the scheme. “Expanding trade among African countries would not only promote economic cooperation but also strengthen relationships among nations and contribute to peace and security across the continent,” he said. The minister’s appeal comes as Kogi State seeks to position itself as a centre for regional commerce, industrial production and agricultural processing, leveraging its geographical location and natural resources. Welcoming participants, Governor Ahmed Usman Ododo said the state’s location at the confluence of Rivers Niger and Benue, agricultural resources, solid mineral deposits and road networks connecting major economic centres offered significant opportunities for trade and investment. Ododo said his administration’s 32-year development plan was designed to translate these advantages into sustainable economic prosperity. He disclosed that the proposed Ajaokuta Free Trade Zone, Agro-Processing Zone and Kogi International Airport were among the strategic projects being pursued to attract investors, expand production capacity and connect local businesses to international markets. item.title: How I met my wife 22 years ago – Actor Odunlade Adekola
item.description: Nollywood actor Odunlade Adekola has celebrated his wife, Ruth Abosede Adekola, on her birthday, recalling how he approached her and expressed his intention to marry her about 22 years ago. The 49-year-old actor shared the tribute in an Instagram post on Monday, reflecting on the beginning of their relationship and his decision to make her his wife. “I saw Madam Ruth Abosede Adekola about 22 years ago!” he wrote. “I walked up to her and said, ‘My friend! I see what I want in you. Can you be mine?’” Adekola, who described Ruth as the mother of his children, also recalled getting fully engaged to her two decades ago. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Odunlade Adekola (@odunomoadekola) “20 years ago, I got fully engaged to my baby, the MOTHER of our KINGS. Deaconess Ruth Abosede Adekola,” he added. The actor further described his wife as his “number one fan”, reaffirming his love and commitment to her while promising to cherish her for the rest of his life. He also offered prayers for God’s continued favour upon their household, wished her a happy birthday and urged his followers to join him in celebrating her. Adekola, over the years, has established himself in Nollywood as an actor, screenwriter, film producer and director. item.title: Ogun 2027: Adebutu dismisses exclusion from INEC list
item.description: ……receives over 1,000 APC defectors into PDP in Ogun By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) governorship candidate in Ogun State, Hon. Oladipupo Adebutu, has dismissed the omission of his name from the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) list of governorship candidates as a temporary distraction, insisting that the development would not derail his ambition to contest the 2027 governorship election. Adebutu spoke on Monday while receiving more than 1,000 defectors from the All Progressives Congress (APC) into the PDP at the party’s State Secretariat in Abeokuta, the Ogun State capital. The defectors, led by a former member of the House of Representatives, Hon. Segun William, were received by Adebutu alongside prominent PDP leaders, including the party’s Ogun Central senatorial candidate, Iyabo Obasanjo. Addressing the gathering, Adebutu expressed confidence that the controversy surrounding his omission from INEC’s list would eventually be resolved, maintaining that he remained a bona fide member of the PDP. He argued that his political history and participation in elections under the party’s platform over the past two decades were sufficient evidence of his loyalty, challenging those questioning his membership to produce evidence of when he allegedly defected. “I have been the candidate of the PDP for the last 20 years, in every election cycle. My question is: at what stage did I leave or vacate the party? Where is the proof that, for one day, I have even visited the APC office, let alone joined the party?” he asked. The PDP chieftain further disclosed that he played an active role in organising and financing the party’s recent membership registration exercise in Ogun State, which, according to him, recorded more than 19,800 members. He said his registration number in the exercise was 1536, describing the development as further evidence of his continued membership of the opposition party. Adebutu alleged that the controversy surrounding his name on the INEC list was an attempt to distract the opposition and disenfranchise voters, but assured party supporters that the PDP would remain focused on its political activities. “The controversy surrounding my name on the INEC list is an attempt to distract the opposition and disenfranchise voters. But I assure our supporters that this party will not lose focus,” he said. He also disclosed that the party had intensified its grassroots mobilisation across the state, revealing that its campaign team had visited 12 of Ogun State’s 20 local government areas and more than 140 of the 236 wards. According to him, the mobilisation exercise would continue despite what he described as efforts to distract the party from its political objectives. “We have visited 12 of the 20 local governments. Of the 236 wards, we have visited over 140. Tomorrow, we continue again because we know that the trick is to get us distracted. We will not be distracted. We will keep our eyes on the ball,

item.title: 2027: 42 trade unions in Delta back Tinubu, Oborevwori, Dafinone
item.description: ‎ ‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ‎ ‎ABUJA — AHEAD of the January 16, elections, a coalition of 42 trade unions in Delta State has pledged support for the re-election of President Bola Tinubu, Governor Sheriff Oborevwori and all All Progressives Congress (APC) candidates in the 2027 general elections. ‎ ‎The coalition, operating under the Delta State Informal Sector Association, comprises over 120,000 artisans and informal sector workers across the state. ‎ ‎The group pledged its allegiance at the weekend when its leadership paid a solidarity visit to Senator representing Delta Central Senatorial District, Ede Dafinone. ‎ ‎While receiving the representatives of the association, Senator Dafinone described their coming together under one platform as a significant step towards strengthening grassroots mobilisation and political engagement. ‎ ‎He commended the various trade unions for uniting under the association and appreciated them for reaffirming their support for Tinubu, Oborevwori, his own re-election and the success of all APC candidates in the 2027 elections. ‎ ‎The senator said “this development reflects a shared commitment to strengthening our party’s political structures through effective grassroots mobilisation and sustained engagement with different segments of society.” ‎ ‎He also acknowledged the importance of the informal sector, noting that the coalition’s broad membership provided an avenue for deeper engagement with artisans, traders and other workers across Delta State. item.title: NDLEA, Australian police sign pact against drug cartels
item.description: ….Marwa describes agreement as declaration of war on transnational traffickers By Kingsley Omonobi ABUJA — The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) and the Australian Federal Police (AFP) have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to strengthen cooperation against transnational drug trafficking networks operating along the Nigeria-Australia route. The agreement, signed at the NDLEA national headquarters in Abuja on Monday, November 2, 2026, formalises existing cooperation between the two agencies into a structured strategic partnership. Speaking at the ceremony, NDLEA Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, Brig. Gen. Mohamed Buba Marwa (retd.), described the agreement as “a declaration of war against transnational drug cartels that think they can hide between continents”. He expressed confidence that the partnership would make the Australia-Nigeria drug route hostile and unprofitable for traffickers, leveraging the AFP’s global reach and the NDLEA’s operational capacity. Under the agreement, the agencies will cooperate in four key areas: information and intelligence sharing, joint and coordinated operations, capacity building and professional development, and controlled delivery. Marwa said the pact came at a time when drug trafficking had become increasingly transnational, organised and sophisticated, with Nigerian organised crime groups allegedly linked to the Australia-Pacific drug route, particularly in the trafficking of methamphetamine and cocaine. “Nigeria is being exploited as a transit and sourcing hub, but no single country can fight this alone,” he said. He expressed hope that the agreement would lead to major joint seizures, arrests of high-value targets and successful controlled deliveries, adding that both agencies looked forward to its immediate implementation. Citing recent operations, the NDLEA boss disclosed that the agency had seized 184.5 kilogrammes of cocaine intended for export and dismantled four methamphetamine laboratories in recent months, where Mexican nationals were allegedly embedded. He said one of the laboratories yielded seizures valued at more than $360 million. Marwa also cited the dismantling of a Switzerland-based cartel allegedly linked to a Nigerian, Simon Amadi, following more than a year of joint operations involving the United States Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA), as well as French, Greek and Swiss police. He said the cartel’s assets in Nigeria had also been targeted. In her remarks, leader of the AFP delegation, Ms Sandra Booth, said tackling drug trafficking required a whole-of-society approach. She commended the NDLEA for addressing different aspects of the problem, from prevention to enforcement, and described its international partnerships as commendable. Booth said the agreement would serve as a “force multiplier” in the fight against drug trafficking. item.title: Carrick shrugs off Man Utd sack talk ahead of Roma match
item.description: Michael Carrick brushed off suggestions he has just two games left as Manchester United boss as he prepares his underperforming side for Tuesday’s Champions League clash against Roma. Carrick’s position at Old Trafford is increasingly precarious following Saturday’s 2-0 defeat at Chelsea, which extended United’s winless run in all competitions to nine games — they last had a longer such sequence in 1984. Former United and England midfielder Carrick was asked at his pre-match press conference on Monday whether he felt he had just two games remaining at the helm — against Roma and Aston Villa. The Villa match on Sunday comes just before an international break, potentially giving the United hierarchy an opportunity to make a managerial change. “No, not at all,” said the 45-year-old, in his first full season in charge. “If you look into the future, you never know what’s going to happen. “I don’t know what’s going to happen. That doesn’t change the way I feel, how we’re preparing for the game tomorrow. “I’m actually really looking forward to the game, can’t wait for the game tomorrow. You might think I’m crazy with the results we’ve had and what’s going on, but I genuinely can’t wait.” Carrick also said he had “no concerns” over the commitment of out-of-form Argentine centre-back Lisandro Martinez, who was sent off in United’s defeat at Stamford Bridge. The defender had previously criticised club chiefs over a lack of investment in the squad. “Things happen in football, sometimes you do things, sometimes you make decisions, sometimes you make mistakes, sometimes it goes well for you, but the commitment is not an issue for sure,” said Carrick. – Dressing-room mood – The United head coach insisted the dressing room was in “a good place” despite the club’s terrible start to the season. “Perception is a funny thing. You can make things look all sorts of different ways and think about all sorts of different things,” he said. “I’ve said it before, the commitment of the players to the club, to me, to each other, I don’t question that at all. We need to play better, we can make better decisions, but commitment is not a thing at all.” United are just one place above the Premier League relegation zone after taking a mere seven points from their nine matches so far this season. And they are 20th in the Champions League table following a dismal 4-1 defeat away at Como last month. Only the top 24 teams will progress beyond the league phase. But midfielder Kobbie Mainoo, sitting alongside Carrick at Monday’s press conference, said United could turn things around. “We’ve not had the results we’ve wanted,” said the 21-year-old. “But we need to look forward now. There’s big, big games ahead and I feel like we’re one win away from changing that.” Carrick has fond memories of facing Roma as a member of Alex Ferguson’s team, scoring twice in United’s 7-1 quarter-final second-leg triumph in the Champions League in 2007. “It was a magical night, I have to say,” he recalled

item.title: Miner dies in pit collapse in Plateau
item.description: By Golok Nanmwa JOS — A 35-year-old miner, identified as Ibrahim Jabir, has died following the collapse of a mining pit at Asaradan village in Jos East Local Government Area of Plateau State. The incident reportedly occurred at about 12:10 a.m. on Sunday, November 1, 2026, trapping the miner in the collapsed pit. A resident of Jos East, Peter Ajik, who confirmed the incident to newsmen in Jos on Monday, said Jabir died at the scene. “The victim, Ibrahim Jabir, died in the incident. The incident happened around 12:10 a.m. when the mining pit collapsed,” Ajik said. He described the incident as another reminder of the dangers associated with mining activities, particularly where adequate safety measures are not observed. Ajik urged miners to take safety precautions seriously and called on relevant authorities to intensify monitoring of mining activities in the area. He also said security operatives responded to a distress call following the collapse. “We are appealing to the relevant authorities to intensify monitoring of mining activities in the area and ensure that safety measures are strictly observed to prevent further loss of lives,” he said. Efforts to reach security operatives for further details were unsuccessful as of the time of filing this report. The post Miner dies in pit collapse in Plateau appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Democrats, Trump hold final rallies before midterm elections
item.description: Donald Trump and his Republican Party will make last-gasp pitches to US midterm voters Monday to hold back a predicted Democrat wave that could sweep Congress and impose tight political constraints on the president for the first time in two years. For his closing arguments, Trump chose a speech in Washington at the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool — a landmark that has become synonymous with the 80-year-old president’s controversial drive to redevelop the US capital. “We’re going to win,” he said on Sunday. Democrats, meanwhile, prepared a round of final rallies — including by star Democratic Senate candidates James Talarico in Texas and Adam Hamilton in Kansas — which will cap a campaign of breathtaking tension and bitterness. Polls are largely in their favor, showing that Democrats are poised to take the majority from Republicans in the House of Representatives and have a real shot at winning the currently Republican Senate. Even winning just the House would mean Democrats have voting power over the federal budget and would lead powerful committees able to investigate alleged corruption under Trump, the Epstein files and other explosive issues. The loss of total Republican dominance would push Trump into a lame-duck period, with high inflation at home, the sputtering war against Iran, and hostile Democratic investigations into his activities in Washington. But a decade into the Trump era, Democrats are wary about predictions of victory. “Nauseously optimistic,” Democratic Senator Raphael Warnock told CNN to describe the mood. – Scorched earth – Democrats are also facing late internal divisions, with left-wing candidates clashing at times with the party’s establishment. In a startling display of infighting on Sunday, Democratic congresswoman Haley Stevens in Michigan endorsed Republican candidate Mike Rogers against left-wing progressive candidate Abdul El-Sayed in her state’s key Senate race. Stevens, who lost a bruising primary to El-Sayed in August despite being backed by the Democratic establishment, struggled to explain her decision in an interview with CNN. Trump’s Republicans have fought a political scorched-earth campaign, painting Democrats as communists and openly branding El-Sayed, who is Muslim, as a terrorist. Addressing a crowd in Iowa on Sunday, Trump said Democrats are “extreme and dangerous radicals” who will “steal your wealth” and let in migrants to “ransack, rape and plunder.” But polls show Americans souring on Trump’s wrecking-ball act. While the House seems highly likely to turn Democratic, the battle for the Senate is up in the air. Only a third of the Senate’s 100 seats are being contested in these midterms, and few of the races were seen as favorable to Democrats. To win the upper chamber, Democrats must flip seats in states the president carried by double digits two years before. This has only happened five times in midterm elections since 1990. item.title: Ebola outbreak kills more than 5,300 people – Africa CDC
item.description: Africa’s latest Ebola outbreak has killed more than 5,300 people, the vast majority of them in the Democratic Republic of Congo, according to the continent’s top health agency. In mid-May, the DRC declared its 17th Ebola outbreak, a deadly disease transmitted through contact with bodily fluids that causes haemorrhagic fever and has killed more than 15,000 people in Africa over the past 50 years. According to data shared with AFP by the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) on Monday, the outbreak, which has spread to other countries on the continent, has killed 5,376 people — 5,372 in the DRC and two each in Kenya and Uganda. A total of 10,444 cases have been confirmed, with a fatality rate of more than 50 percent. The virus has crossed borders several times in recent months. Neighbouring Uganda recorded 20 cases, almost all involving people who had travelled from the DRC, before being declared Ebola-free in August. In October, Kenya recorded nine infections, marking the first time the country had reported an Ebola case. That same month, Nigeria, Africa’s most populous country, reported an Ebola case involving a 42-year-old Swiss woman whose husband works at the Swiss embassy in Abuja. The couple had travelled to Uganda before returning to Nigeria. The outbreak is caused by the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola, for which no approved vaccine or treatment is currently available. In recent weeks, clinical trials have begun with the Ervebo vaccine, which has proved effective against the more common Zaire strain of the virus. item.title: We’re facing challenges, hostility around us — Tinubu
item.description: –Says his prayer for wisdom, resilience to continue serving Nigeria has been granted –Reaffirms commitment to Project Nigeria By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA — PRESIDENT Bola Tinubu has said that although the country is facing challenges and hostility, Nigeria will overcome them through faith in God Almighty. President Tinubu, who is in Mecca for a holy obligation, said he asked for wisdom and resilience to continue serving the people, and that his prayer has been granted, just as it was before the 2023 election, when God answered him. The President made the remarks on Monday while reflecting on his spiritual journey to the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia to perform Umrah, during which the Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques of Makkah and Madinah, King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, granted him the rare privilege of leading Nigeria’s delegation to pray inside the Holy Ka’abah. He reaffirmed his determination to build a prosperous nation, invest in the future of young Nigerians, and pursue development in line with the will of Almighty God and the aspirations of the people. At the Ka’abah, President Tinubu offered prayers of gratitude to Almighty Allah for the privilege of serving as Nigeria’s President and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces. Sheikh Dahlulah Muthawal of Masjid al-Haram led the President into the Ka’abah. President Tinubu thanked the Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques, King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, and Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman for granting him and members of his Nigerian delegation the opportunity to enter the Holy Ka’abah in Makkah and offer prayers to Almighty Allah. The President described the honour as a historic and deeply cherished spiritual experience, reflecting the longstanding bonds of friendship, mutual respect and cooperation between Nigeria and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. “I want to say a big thank you for the faith and recognition. I can’t believe the fencing of the Ka’abah is in green, white and green, which reminds us of our Nigerian identity. “I thank the Crown Prince and all the administrators of the Holy Land. I thank them for the hospitality and recognition given to me as the leader of the delegation and of the country. “We are all facing challenges and hostility around us, but we will overcome them with faith in God Almighty. I am grateful forever. I thank the King and the Crown Prince. “It is an honour that I enjoyed, and it is gracious of them to have allowed me to enter inside the Ka’abah. This is history,” the President said. I know that prayer has been granted. Before the 2023 election, I did the same thing. I asked Allah to bless my Umrah then, and He did. item.title: Using 1963 Fire Act to fight 2026 fires unacceptable, FG declares
item.description: .Unveils vision of new fire and rescue service .Cuts response time to 15 minutes, 119 lives saved By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The Federal Government has said it makes no sense to continue to rely on a fire law enacted in 1963 to tackle fire emergencies in 2026, as it prepares to send a new Federal Fire and Rescue Service Act to President Bola Tinubu soon for assent. Minister of Interior, Dr Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, said this on Monday in Abuja at the opening ceremony and stakeholders’ conference of the 2026 National Fire Safety Week. “You cannot have a Federal Fire Service Act of 1963, and you think it would be 2026-compliant. It doesn’t make sense” the minister said. He said the old law denies firefighters the powers they need to do their work. “If the law does not give you the power to do something, no matter how good that action is, once you do it, it becomes illegal. There is no right way of doing something that is legally wrong,” he said. Tunji-Ojo said the review of the Act had been completed and the new bill should be laid before the President in a matter of days. He said it was the first time in 63 years that any government had taken up the task. The minister said the new law would open the sector to private sector intervention and move the service beyond firefighting. “When it comes to hazards, fire is only one of the hazards. Even flood, water can be hazardous,” he said. He said he wanted a Federal Fire Service that responds to medical emergencies, floods, chemical spills, toxic materials, bomb attacks and earthquakes. He added that fire suppression was only one of about twenty responsibilities of fire services elsewhere. “I want to see a Federal Fire Service whose specialisation is rescue operations,” he said. Tunji-Ojo also called for stronger fire inspection and code enforcement, with volunteer fire marshals in every district and town. He said the service should work with education authorities to make rescue skills part of school curricula. “If anything happens, maybe somebody faints, what percentage of Nigerians can even do a simple resuscitation process?” he asked. The minister said the service should also investigate emergencies beyond fire incidents, and should chair a council of fire and rescue services to coordinate policy across the country. On performance, the minister said the average response time to fire incidents was between 32 and 35 minutes when the administration came into office. He said it now stands at 15 minutes, 22 seconds. He said that as of August, 119 lives were saved with no life lost to fire in 36 incidents nationwide. “There is a lot he’s working under the old law, so there’s a limit to how well he can do this,” Tunji-Ojo said of the Controller-General of the Federal Fire Service, Olumode Samuel Adeyemi. The minister said the National Fire Academy was 85 per cent complete and would be running by the end of the year, with commissioning expected in December. item.title: 2027: Give Tinubu, Otu another term, Shettima tells Cross River
item.description: …says authority belongs to the people …Bakassi Deep seaport will be one Nigeria’s maritime gateway By Ike Uchechukwu, CALABAR Nigeria’s vice president, Senator Kashim Shettima, on Monday, held out the promise of a deep seaport in Bakassi and the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway to Cross River voters, asking them to renew the mandate of President Bola Tinubu and Governor Bassey Otu in 2027. Representing the President at the APC Presidential Campaign rally at the U.J. Esuene Stadium, Shettima brought the President’s greetings and thanked the people for standing by the administration. “Over the past three years, you have shown us support, and you have resisted the lies and propaganda intended to misrepresent us,” he said. He described the relationship with the people of Cross River and Nogeria at large as “an alliance of prosperity, an alliance of opportunity”. He said the APC was seeking votes for Tinubu, Governor Otu, and candidates for the National Assembly and the State House of Assembly. “We are asking because authority belongs to the people. Those entrusted with authority must return with an account of their stewardship.” Turning to the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway, he said the project would “connect coastal communities” and “ease the movement of goods and people.” He added that it would expand tourism, attract investors and create thousands of direct and indirect jobs. On the Bakassi Deep Seaport, he said the project had received federal government approval. “When completed, it will become an international maritime gateway. It will attract shipping companies. It will generate employment,” he said. He said the two projects were part of a plan to make Cross River a major beneficiary of the government’s maritime economy agenda. The vice president also spoke about education, saying the government’s student financing intervention would drive human capital development in the state. He said it would give relief to parents and widen access to higher education so that no parent would be forced to abandon a child’s schooling for lack of funds. Shettima praised the party faithful at the rally, saying they were “chosen by you, endorsed by you.” He asked them to vote for the APC “from top to bottom” in the 2027 elections. “You, the people, are the purpose and authority of you,” he declared. item.title: 2027: Critics of Rainbow Coalition incapable of uniting their own families – Wike
item.description: …Tells FCT residents, ‘election day is not for market or fishing’ By Omeiza Ajayi, Abuja Minister of the Federal Capital Territory FCT, Nyesom Wike, has said politicians who deny the existence of the Rainbow Coalition lack the capacity to unite even their own families and communities. Wike spoke on Monday in Abuja at the commissioning of the Gwagwalada Civic Centre and an interactive session with stakeholders of the All Progressives Congress APC and the Peoples Democratic Party PDP in Gwagwalada Area Council. The minister said the coalition, which brings together political stakeholders from both parties, was formed in the interest of unity, cooperation and development in the FCT. “Some greedy and selfish politicians do not understand what we call unity. They have no capacity to hold their space, they have no capacity to even hold their families, and they have no capacity to hold their communities. So they can open their mouths and say there is no Rainbow Coalition,” he said. Wike challenged critics of the alliance to explain why political leaders who once disagreed could not come together to pursue common interests. He described the development in Gwagwalada as a departure from the politics of confrontation, insisting that the FCT needed cooperation rather than needless political hostility. Commending political leaders in the area for setting aside their differences, he said their decision showed that the collective interest of the people outweighed individual political ambition. Wike also urged residents not to repeat what he described as the mistake of the 2023 general elections and called for credible representation at the National Assembly. The minister canvassed support for a former senator, Philip Aduda, and other candidates endorsed by the coalition, saying political representatives must be accessible and familiar with their constituents. Wike also declared support for the re-election of President Bola Tinubu and urged residents to turn their endorsements into votes in 2027. “On the day of the election, it will not be a day for market or fishing. It is the day all of us have decided to come together and demonstrate our strength through our votes. Go to the polling units, districts and communities and mobilise the people to vote for Bola Ahmed Tinubu,” he said. Earlier, the FCT APC Chairman, Ishaku Tanko Yamawo, described the gathering as historic, saying Wike’s intervention had brought together leaders who previously operated on opposing sides. The FCT PDP Chairman, Alhaji Ismaila Mohammed Dogara, praised Wike for his development interventions, particularly the revival of a project abandoned for 16 years in Gwagwalada. The Aguma of Gwagwalada, Alhaji Muhammadu Magaji, also commended Wike’s contributions to the development of the territory. He said the revival of the abandoned project underscored the importance of continuity in governance.
